title: Waves
line: The primes are made of waves
summary: What the hypothesis says, where the zeros show up in a count of primes, and how the proof turns “nothing to the right of the line” into “everything on it”.
story: The goal is fixed first. `Statements.lean` writes the hypotheses in Mathlib’s own terms, and `Main.lean` derives all five headline theorems from a single result, `grh`: no Dirichlet L-function vanishes to the right of the line Re s = 1/2.

The step from “nothing to the right” to “everything on the line” is the mirror symmetry of zeros (`New/Main`, `Lib/Analytic/ZeroSymmetry`). A zero off the line would have a twin on the other side, and one of the two would sit to the right.

The waves enter through a weighted count of primes. `PrimeError` defines its remainder R_q. Its transform has poles exactly at zeros of L-functions, so each zero contributes a wave to the count. `PrimeNumberTheorem` shows that R_q tends to 0, which the proof uses at a far-out second cut-off.

elsewhere.label: Tam Nguyen Duc: the proof in four levels

modules.title: From non-vanishing in Re s > 1/2 to zeros on the critical line
modules.note:
The last step: the usual forms of the hypothesis follow from `DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf`,
the non-vanishing of all Dirichlet L-functions in `re s > 1 / 2`, by the symmetry `s ↦ 1 - s` of the
zeros.

* `New.zeros_on_line`: the zeros of `L(s, χ)` in `0 < re s < 1` have `re s = 1 / 2`.
* `New.zeta_zeros_on_line`: the nontrivial zeros of `ζ` have `re s = 1 / 2`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the passage from the half-plane to the critical line by the functional equation. The
non-vanishing itself is `New.grh`.

modules.title: Zeros of L(s, χ) and of L(1 − s, χ⁻¹)
modules.note:
`New.gammaFactor_eq_zero_or_LFunction_one_sub_eq_zero` shows that a zero `s` of L(·, χ) with
`s.re ≠ 0` and `s ≠ 1` is either a pole of `χ.gammaFactor` or gives the zero `1 - s` of L(·, χ⁻¹),
extending the symmetry given by the functional equation from primitive to all Dirichlet characters.
modules.literature:
Known result: the symmetry of the zeros, a consequence of the functional equation for Dirichlet
L-functions. Source: Montgomery and Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I, 2007, Corollaries 10.3
and 10.8.

modules.title: A weighted prime-counting error term and its poles at zeros of L-functions
modules.group: From a one-sided bound to the zeros
modules.note:
Let `d` be a prime and `χ_K = (·/d)` the Legendre symbol. We study the remainder `R_q` of a weighted
sum over the prime powers `n ≡ 1` modulo `q` with `χ_K(n) ≠ 1`. Its Laplace transform sees the zeros
of the Dirichlet `L`-functions modulo `q` and of their twists by `χ_K`.

* `New.lambdaKResidueClass`: the weight `λ(n) = Λ(n) (1 - χ_K(n))` on `n ≡ 1` modulo `q`; it is
  nonnegative.
* `New.logDerivMean`: the mean `G_q` over the characters `ψ` modulo `q` of the differences of the
  logarithmic derivatives of `New.entireL (New.quadTwist ψ d)` and `New.entireL ψ`, less `1 / φ(q)`.
* `New.primeRemainder`: `R_q(x) = ∑_{n ≤ x} λ(n) (1/n - 1/x) - log x / φ(q) - re G_q(1)`.
* `New.LSeries_lambdaKResidueClass_eq_add_logDerivMean`: for odd `d` prime to `q`, the Dirichlet
  series of `λ` is `s / (φ(q) (s - 1)) + G_q(s)` in `re s > 1`.
* `New.isPolar_primeRemainder`: for `d ≡ 7` modulo `8` prime to `q`, the transform of
  `v ↦ R_q(e ^ v)` has at most simple poles in `re s > 0`, none at `1`, and at `s ≠ 1` with the
  residue `(n(s) - n'(s)) / (φ(q) s (1 - s))`, where `n(s)` and `n'(s)` are the sums of the orders
  at `s` of these `L`-functions and of their twists.

Here `New.entireL ψ` is `L(s, ψ)`, times `s - 1` if `ψ` is principal, `New.quadTwist ψ d` is the
character `ψ χ_K`, and `New.chowlaSelbergConst d` is, for odd `d`, `γ - re L'/L(1, χ_K)`, with `γ`
Euler's constant.
modules.literature:
The transform of a weighted prime sum in a residue class is computed by orthogonality of characters
and partial summation. Source: Davenport, Multiplicative Number Theory.

modules.title: The prime number theorem for the remainders `R_q`
modules.group: From a one-sided bound to the zeros
modules.note:
Let `d` be a prime and `q ≥ 1`. The remainder `R_q(y)` is an integral of the error `𝓔_q(t)` in the
weighted count (`primeRemainder_eq_integral_countError_sub`), so it varies slowly. For odd `d` prime
to `q` its absolute value is at most `(log y) ^ (-B)` for all large `y`, for every natural number
`B`; so it tends to `0`, which characterises the constant `c_q` in its definition.

Notions from other files:
* `lambdaKResidueClass d q n` is `λ(n) = Λ(n) (1 - (n/d))` for `n ≡ 1` mod `q`, and `0` for other
  `n`.
* `entireL ψ` is `L(s, ψ)`, multiplied by `s - 1` if `ψ` is principal; `quadTwist ψ d` is the
  product of `ψ` and the Legendre symbol `(·/d)`.
* `logDerivMean d q` is the function `G_q` that continues `∑ λ(n) n ^ (-s) - s / (φ(q) (s - 1))`
  when `d` is odd and prime to `q`.
* `primeRemainder d q y` is `R_q(y) = ∑_{n ≤ y} λ(n) (1/n - 1/y) - log y / φ(q) - c_q` with
  `c_q = re G_q(1)`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions with an error term that saves every
power of the logarithm. It is a case of the Siegel–Walfisz theorem. Source: Montgomery and Vaughan,
Multiplicative Number Theory I, 2007, Cor. 11.19. Form here: the modulus is fixed, and the count is
the smoothed sum `∑_{n ≤ y} λ(n) (1/n - 1/y)` over the prime powers `n ≡ 1` mod `q`; for `d ≡ 3` mod
`4` the primes that split in `ℚ(√-d)` have weight zero.
role: The prime number theorem for the remainder of the prime sum, used at the second cut-off.
